title: Hind Daughter of Al-Nu'man and Al-Hajjaj (മലയാളം)

keywords: hind daughter of al-nu'man and al-hajjaj
full_text:
Princess Hind, daughter of Al-Nu'man, was celebrated throughout Iraq as a woman of peerless beauty, noble ancestry, and formidable intellect. When the fierce and tyrannical governor Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf forced her into marriage through his political power, Hind accepted with cold, dignified disdain, treating the tyrant as an uncouth usurper.

One afternoon, sitting before her mirror in the palace, Hind recited aloud an exquisite satirical verse:
'Can a noble Arabian gazelle of pedigree blood
Be mated with an ox that wallows in the mud?'

Al-Hajjaj overheard the verse from the corridor, flew into a furious temper, and sent his servant with two hundred thousand dirhams to divorce her on the spot, saying: 'Tell her she is divorced in three words, and give her this gold!'

The servant delivered the message. Hind smiled with royal composure, tossed the two hundred thousand dirhams to the servant as a tip, and replied:
'Tell Al-Hajjaj: By heavens, I was never honored by his union, nor am I grieved by his departure!'

When the Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik in Damascus heard of her unmatched wit and regal pride, he was enchanted and sent a royal proposal to wed her.

Hind agreed, but made one mischievous condition: that Al-Hajjaj himself must lead her bridal camel on foot from Iraq to Damascus!

The Caliph commanded it, and the proud tyrant was forced to walk on foot holding the camel’s bridle all the way to Syria. Hind tossed a gold dinar into the dust and called down: 'Ho, camel-driver! Pick up that gold coin!' Al-Hajjaj picked it up and said: 'It is a dinar.' Hind laughed: 'Praise be to heaven! The camel-driver has picked up a coin, but dropped an entire kingdom of pride!'
moral: Razor-sharp wit, poetic pride, and moral dignity disarm the fiercest tyrant without the clash of swords. [ML]
